findings.mechanism: The focus side-turn carrier contacts the 32:16 HFT-attributed bodily withdrawal, literal-side, calling, and Lordship roles. The counterimage revalues the focus movement through the direction it takes, rather than treating motion or a side as intrinsically culpable.
findings.reader_payoff: A bodily image of turning aside becomes morally precise: the reader attends to what the body leaves and what it faces.
findings.containment: This is an attributed cross-root spatial counterimage, not lexical equivalence between 32:16 roots and the focus verb. Context morphology is absent. The B001 side extension survives only alongside its core; the comparison does not claim sideward devotion is the lexical meaning of the focus verb.

epistemic.reason: The exact 32:16 surface and focus QAC carrier support the spatial contact; the HFT word-index/root roles remain attributed and the cross-root relation is interpretive.
